title: Stock Market Update: Profit Taking Pushes S&P Slightly Lower
text:
Moving the Market
Investors take some profits following four straight record-setting sessions
Stocks drop to new lows following reports that President Trump wants to impose tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods as early as next week
FAANG names outperform, helping to keep losses in check Profit Taking Pushes S&P Slightly Lower 30-Aug-18 13:00 ET Dow -65.38 at 26059.19, Nasdaq +16.78 at 8126.49, S&P -3.72 at 2910.06
[BRIEFING.COM] Stocks have taken a step back today as investors engage in some profit taking following four straight record-setting days on Wall Street. The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average are down 0.2% and 0.3%, respectively, but the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite is outperforming with a slim gain of 0.1%.
Today's losses are broad-based with eight of eleven sectors in negative territory. The lightly-weighted materials space (-1.3%) is at the bottom of the sector standings, and the energy (-0.7%) and financials (-0.5%) sectors are also showing relative weakness. However, no other laggard is down more than 0.4%.
On the flip side, the top-weighted information technology sector (+0.2%) is up modestly, helped by the outperformance of FAANG names like Facebook (FB 179.42, +3.51), Apple (AAPL 225.80, +2.81), and Netflix (NFLX 374.04, +6.00), which are up between 1.2% and 2.0% apiece. Apple was helped by investing legend Warren Buffett, who said in a CNBC interview that he's recent bought more shares.
Meanwhile, Amazon (AMZN 2023.06, +24.96) is also having a solid outing, up 1.3% and crossing the psychologically-important $2000 mark for the first time ever.
In earnings news, Dollar Tree (DLTR 81.97, -12.48) has tumbled 13.2% after reporting worse-than-expected earnings, and Abercrombie & Fitch (ANF 22.70, -4.53) has plunged 16.6% despite beating profit estimates. Conversely, Signet Jewelers (SIG 68.43, +13.78) has spiked 25.2%, hitting a nine-month high, after beating both top and bottom line estimates and raising its guidance for FY19.
Looking at other markets, U.S. Treasuries have moved higher today, sending yields lower across the curve, with the benchmark 10-yr yield down two basis points at 2.86%. The U.S. Dollar Index is up 0.3% at 94.72, looking to end a four-session losing streak, and WTI crude futures are up 0.6% at $69.92/bbl.
In Washington, NAFTA negotiations remain in focus as the U.S. and Mexico try to bring Canada onto the bilateral trade deal they reached on Monday. Although there are reportedly a number of tricky issues still to work through, both President Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau expressed optimism on Wednesday that a deal could get done by the end of the week.
Reviewing today's economic data, which included July Personal Income, Personal Spending, and PCE Prices and the weekly Initial Claims report: Personal income climbed 0.3% in July (Briefing.com consensus +0.4%) following an unrevised increase of 0.4% in June. Meanwhile, personal spending rose 0.4% (Briefing.com consensus +0.4%) following an unrevised increase of 0.4%. The PCE Price Index rose 0.1% in July, and the core PCE Price Index, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.2% (Briefing.com consensus +0.2%). The key takeaway from the report is twofold: (1) the spending increase puts Q3 GDP on a solid growth track and (2) the year-over-year increase in the PCE Price Index (+2.3% vs. +2.2% prior) and the core PCE Price Index (+2.0% vs. +1.9% prior) will keep the Federal Reserve on its tightening track in September. The latest weekly initial jobless claims count totaled 213,000, while the Briefing.com consensus expected a reading of 214,000. Today's tally was above the unrevised prior week count of 210,000. As for continuing claims, they declined to 1.708 million from a revised count of 1.728 million (from 1.727 million). The key takeaway from the report is the recognition that the four-week moving average of 212,250 for initial claims is the lowest since December 13, 1969, underscoring the strength in the labor market.
